subject.title: fix(approvals): fail closed plugin tool gates

question: Should OpenClaw disable the shipped plugin `timeoutBehavior: "allow"` fallback in this release while retaining the field as a deprecated no-op for one release train?
rationale: The implementation correctly strengthens an execution-authorization boundary, but the timing of an intentional shipped plugin behavior change requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept fail-closed now
options.body: Ignore the fallback immediately, retain the warning and one-train deprecation shell, and remove the field on the documented schedule.

options.title: Stage the cutover
options.body: Preserve allow-on-timeout temporarily while landing approval-ID binding, exact verdict filtering, and one-shot consumption separately.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed now
recommendation.body: Ignore the fallback immediately, retain the warning and one-train deprecation shell, and remove the field on the documented schedule.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent approval-stack work spans the central gateway runtime, related security hardening, and the compatibility boundary requiring this decision.
